claims.text: The starting high-entropy nanoalloy has a single-phase FCC structure.
Introducing a small amount of oxide dispersion can improve the structural stability of a high-entropy nanoalloy at high temperature.
Introducing a small amount of oxide dispersion can improve the chemical stability of a high-entropy nanoalloy at high temperature.
The introduced oxide dispersion is the structural mediator of the proposed stabilization.
Oxide dispersions can pin grain boundaries in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Oxide dispersions can reduce diffusion in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Grain-boundary pinning and reduced diffusion improve high-temperature stability.
Relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide dispersion, the intervention will reduce the oxidation rate.
Relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide dispersion, the intervention will improve mechanical properties.
The proposed effect should hold at temperatures above 800 degrees Celsius.
Oxide dispersion is effective throughout the stated temperature range above 800 degrees Celsius.
An otherwise comparable high-entropy nanoalloy without oxide dispersion is the proposed control.
The optimal amount and type of oxide and the applicable high-entropy-alloy composition are uncertain.
A finding of no stability improvement in the oxide-containing alloy relative to the oxide-free control would falsify the hypothesis.
